newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: IBCA lowers FNB Southern Africa rating.
newsitem.headline: IBCA lowers FNB Southern Africa rating.

text.p: Ratings agency IBCA said on Tuesday it had cut First National Bank of Southern Africa's (FNB) international individual rating to B/C from B, citing a decline in the bank's performance relative to its peer group.

"Affected by international competition and changing requirements in the domestic market, FNB's profitability has been under pressure leading to a restructuring programme designed to improve competitiveness," IBCA said in a statement.
IBCA reaffirmed FNB's domestic short-term rating of A1+ and long-term rating of AA.
"Domestic ratings still indicate a very low expectation of investment risk in the long-term," the agency said
IBCA said FNB's asset quality had been pressured by control problems in the bank's non-core business and high real interest rates combined with the high level of consumer debt.
"The rise in non-performing lending may lead to an increase in future loan loss reserve requirements," IBCA said.
Interest margins, while wide by international standards, had narrowed rapidly, the agency noted.
IBCA said FNB had successfully diversified its income both geographically and by category, while its asset mix had gradually refocussed on retail consumers, a trend expected to continue.

IBCA said the risk profile of the South African banking sector might be impacted as the local economy remained prone to politically related event risks as it adjusted to the dismantling of manufacturing tarrif protection in line with GATT requirements.
GATT is the General Agreement on Tarrifs and Trade.
FNB's group restructure had consolidated treasury and trading activities, assisting a move toward global risk management.
"In a more volatile market, funding is predominantly wholesale and short-term, but not out of line with that of peers," IBCA said.
